messages:
cheng: RFC follow-up — on-prem package signing + rollback workflow. TL;DR: vendor- and customer-signed artifacts, delta-first patching with full fallback, manifest has signature chain, transfer metadata, and explicit migration hooks. Need ops/security input on key custody, DB migration rollback safety, and sideload verification.

sam: sgtm. quick q — how are deltas produced/delivered for very low-bandwidth sites? some customers have <1Mbps bursts.

cheng: deltas computed on build farm as binary diffs (bsdiff-style). Deliver as small payloads with chunked transfer. If delta generation fails or patch > threshold, installer falls back to full image. manifest includes `diff_available: true|false`, `delta_size`, and sha256 checks for each chunk.

maria: we still left key custody fuzzy in RFC. ops prefers two modes: vendor-signed by default, and customer-signed where customer provides a public key bundle (KMS/HSM). offline signing steps must be auditable and logged. Can we add `trusted_signers` to manifest?

cheng: yes — manifest will include `trusted_signers` (list of key IDs + key type) and `signature_chain` entries per artifact. plan to support detached signatures for large assets so installer can stream-verify.

sam: rollback question — DB migrations are the scary bit. what if a migration isn't reversible?

cheng: recommend two-tier approach: prefer additive, backwards-compatible migrations. For irreversible changes, require explicit migration metadata in manifest with `forward` and `reverse` scripts. If `reverse` is absent, the installer will refuse automatic rollback and will surface a remediation playbook. We expose an `--allow-unsafe-rollback` flag for emergencies which requires multi-signer approval/audit.

maria: ops wants a strict preflight validation step: signatures, disk space, filepaths, permissions, migration script presence, and a DB snapshot check. Also need a `--dry-run` mode that performs all verification without making changes.

deploy-bot: package 2026-03-15-rc2 signed (sha256:8f2b...c4d1) uploaded to staging :white_check_mark:

dilip: delivery model needs to be explicit: (a) pull via mirror/jumpbox, (b) sideload (usb or transfer node). manifest should codify `delivery.method` and `transfer_checks`. for sideload we must mandate transfer verification and device provenance steps.

cheng: agreed. manifest fields: `delivery.method`: "pull"|"sideload", `transfer_checks`: ["sha256","size","signature"], and `sideload_provenance` optional metadata (operator ID, transfer medium, transfer_timestamp). installer refuses apply if checks fail.

maria: CLI UX proposal for ops: compact but explicit. example:

```
# validate only
rdu apply --manifest manifest.json --dry-run

# apply and create rollback marker
rdu apply --manifest manifest.json --create-rollback-marker

# emergency rollback (requires audit tokens)
rdu rollback --to-marker 2026-03-15-00 --allow-unsafe-rollback --audit-token $(cat token)
```

sam: LGTM. we should run a short threat model focused on offline signing + key rotation. @dilip can you lead?

dilip: on it. i'll run a 30m threat-model session next Tue and post notes. Items i'll cover: signing key compromise, replayed deltas, tampered sideload devices, and rollback abuse.

cheng: outstanding questions for RFC update: 1) exact schema for `trusted_signers` and signature formats (detached vs inline), 2) policy for delta size threshold/fallback, 3) concrete preflight checklist to include in manifest, and 4) audit requirements for `--allow-unsafe-rollback`. i'll update the RFC and push a draft with examples.

maria: i'll draft the ops runbook and checklist (preflight, DB snapshot, apply, smoke tests, post-checks) and include sample commands. also adding a short enterprise rollback runbook for legal/compliance signoffs.

sam: we should also add automated tests for the installer: simulate interrupted delta apply, corrupted chunk, missing signature, and failed migration reverse.

cheng: good call. i'll add an integration test matrix to the RFC. thanks all — expect RFC v1.1 tomorrow.

dilip: quick note — for air-gapped customers, consider offering a small verifier binary that runs on the jumpbox to validate manifest and chunks before shuttling to the target network. reduces blast radius.

maria: nice. add that to runbook.

cheng: closing notes: manifest example skeleton and CLI examples will be in RFC update. meeting to review threat model + ops checklist next Tue.
